question: What is the minimum attendance I need in a bachelor course to avoid failing it automatically?
expected_source: Attendance Policy Bachelor Degrees 2026-2027
reference_answer: Students are expected to attend 100% of sessions, but if attendance falls below 80% they receive a fail grade of 0.0 in both the ordinary and the extraordinary call for that course.

question: Does a medical appointment count as a justified absence under the bachelor attendance policy?
expected_source: Attendance Policy Bachelor Degrees 2026-2027
reference_answer: No. Appointments, including medical ones, are not justified absences and count toward the maximum allowance of 20% total absences per course. Hospitalisation of the student or a family member up to the second degree, with official documentation, is a justified reason.

question: How many days do I have to submit documents to justify an absence, and where do I submit them?
expected_source: Attendance Policy Bachelor Degrees 2026-2027
reference_answer: Within seven (7) days, through the Virtual Help Desk to Program management. The system then notifies the student and the faculty within 72 hours whether the absence has been justified.

question: Can my professor approve or justify one of my absences?
expected_source: Attendance Policy Bachelor Degrees 2026-2027
reference_answer: No. Faculty members are not responsible for or authorised to approve or justify absences. All requests must be managed through Program management via the Virtual Help Desk.

question: Will I be able to watch a recording of an in-person class I missed?
expected_source: Attendance Policy Bachelor Degrees 2026-2027
reference_answer: Normally no: recordings of in-person sessions are not made available. Only in very extraordinary circumstances can Program Management grant an exception, based on justified and documented reasons, and then the recording is available for a limited period of 80 days.

question: What happens if I arrive late to a live in-person class?
expected_source: Attendance Policy Bachelor Degrees 2026-2027
expected_location: Student Behavior in the Classroom - Live in-person sessions
reference_answer: Students are not allowed to enter the classroom once the class has begun, nor to leave until the end of the class. A student who arrives late or leaves early is marked absent by the professor.

question: What is the pass mark for a bachelor course and how are the grade bands defined?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes
reference_answer: The pass grade is 5.0 on a 0-10 scale. 0.0-4.9 is Fail, 5.0-6.9 is Pass, 7.0-8.9 is Very Good and 9.0-10 is Excellent.

question: How long does a bachelor professor have to communicate the grade of an assessment instrument?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes
reference_answer: At most fifteen (15) calendar days from the date the assessment instrument was completed during the teaching period, excluding official holidays.

question: How many ECTS credits must a bachelor student pass each academic year to be allowed to continue?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes
reference_answer: At least 70% of the ECTS credits established for that year. Failing to reach the 70% threshold means the student may not continue in the bachelor programme.

question: How many Honors Distinctions can be awarded in a bachelor course?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes
reference_answer: Honors Distinctions equal to 5% of the students enrolled in the same course may be awarded to students with a grade of 9.0 or higher. If fewer than 20 students are enrolled, only one Honors Distinction is granted. A grade above 9.0 alone does not guarantee one.

question: Can I ask for my final exam to be assessed by a board instead of only my professor?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes
reference_answer: Yes, for final examinations or assessment instruments worth more than 50% of the final grade. The student must ask the academic heads, with duly substantiated reasons, at least seven (7) days before the assessment. If granted, the board has at least the course professor and another professor appointed by the academic heads.

question: How many credits can the Academic Compensation Board compensate, and which courses can never be compensated?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes
reference_answer: A student can appeal for core and compulsory courses worth up to a maximum of 5% of the ECTS credits needed to complete the programme. Credits for the Final Project, internships and elective courses can never be compensated.

question: What is the deadline to ask the Rector for an additional examination session?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes
reference_answer: A written, reasoned request must be submitted to the Rector within twenty (20) working days from the date for finalisation of student achievement records in the academic calendar, after exhausting all avenues for grade review and appeal.

question: What is the maximum length of the teaching period in a bachelor academic year?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes
reference_answer: The teaching period in each academic year shall not exceed forty (40) weeks.

question: Who do I report a suspected academic integrity violation to?
expected_source: The Student Code of Conduct
reference_answer: The Program Direction, which is the single entry point for all academic integrity cases and makes the initial assessment of whether the case is within the scope of the Code.

question: Where do I file a discrimination or harassment complaint at IE?
expected_source: The Student Code of Conduct
reference_answer: With the Diversity Office (DO), the single entry point for discrimination and harassment, through the Harassment and Discrimination Intervention Line (HDI Line) platform.

question: On what grounds can I appeal a sanction in an academic integrity case?
expected_source: The Student Code of Conduct
reference_answer: Only if the process deviated from the Code's rules, if new previously unconsidered evidence emerges, or if the sanction is clearly disproportionate to the offence considering aggravating or mitigating circumstances.

question: What is the most severe sanction for a very serious infraction under the Student Code of Conduct?
expected_source: The Student Code of Conduct
reference_answer: Temporal or permanent expulsion from IE University (or any other sanction deemed appropriate by the authority concerned).

question: Does the Student Code of Conduct apply to things I do off campus?
expected_source: The Student Code of Conduct
reference_answer: Generally not, but there are exceptions: conduct connected with an IE University-related programme, event or activity where IE exercised substantial control over the person and the context, and conduct that directly affects the IE Community's welfare or core values, including its reputation, as decided by IE management.

question: If a master's student passes a subject in the extraordinary call, what is the highest grade they can get?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes
reference_answer: The grade is limited to 5.0 (Pass), so a student who passes in the extraordinary call cannot receive more than 5.0.

question: How many business days do master's professors have to communicate grades after an evaluation exercise?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes
reference_answer: A maximum of ten (10) business days after completion of the evaluation exercises.

question: Which master's students may be included in the Dean's List?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes
reference_answer: Students who completed the syllabus of their master's degree and attained an average grade in the top 10% of their group.

question: How are internal US-style grades distributed in master's programmes?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes
reference_answer: Master's directors may apply an internal curve: Honors for the top 15% of the class, Excellence for the next 35%, Proficiency for the next 35%, and Pass for the lowest 15%. Fail is assigned to students below the mean minus two standard deviations. It is for internal use only and not for official certificates.

question: Do master's students who study in Spanish need to prove their English level?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes
reference_answer: Yes. They must obtain an accreditation of an intermediate academic and professional level of spoken and written English to complete the programme, unless English is their native language.

question: What do I have to include when I disclose that I used AI in an assignment?
expected_source: Student Guidelines for Appropriate Use of AI
reference_answer: Identify the specific AI platforms or tools used, explain how they were used (e.g. brainstorming, proofreading), document the prompts used so faculty can evaluate your skills upon request, and clearly indicate any AI-generated visuals with reference to the tool used.

question: What disclosure statement does IE recommend if AI was allowed in an assignment but I chose not to use it?
expected_source: Student Guidelines for Appropriate Use of AI
reference_answer: The recommended statement is that no content generated by AI technologies has been used in this assignment.

question: Can I paste confidential or sensitive information into a free AI tool such as ChatGPT?
expected_source: Student Guidelines for Appropriate Use of AI
reference_answer: No. Students must never use sensitive, private or confidential information, their own or someone else's, with any public or free AI tool, and should read the Terms of Use and manage privacy settings.

question: If I fall below 80% attendance in a bachelor course, what happens to my grade, and could it affect whether I can continue at IE?
expected_source: Attendance Policy Bachelor Degrees 2026-2027;General Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes
expected_location: Failing a course due to attendance;Art. 38.4, Art. 45.7
reference_answer: The student receives a fail grade of 0.0 in both the ordinary and extraordinary call, and both fails appear on the record and count toward the Bachelor Score. The Bachelor Score is the average of all final grades, including failed ones, and students must reach a minimum annual Bachelor Score of 5.0 or they must discontinue their studies at IE regardless of credits passed.

question: A bachelor student submits an assignment containing AI-generated text without disclosing it. How is this classified and what sanctions could follow?
expected_source: Student Guidelines for Appropriate Use of AI;The Student Code of Conduct
expected_location: What happens if you misuse AI? (p. 4);III.1.1; III.2.2; III.3.1 iii
reference_answer: Submitting AI-generated work without proper disclosure is treated as academic misconduct such as plagiarism or cheating and is reviewed under the Student Code of Conduct. Plagiarism is a serious infraction (it can be very serious depending on severity). Sanctions for serious infractions include re-submission, a failing grade in the assignment or the course, or removal from honours lists, and very serious infractions can lead to temporal or permanent expulsion.

question: How do I challenge a final grade in a bachelor course, and what are the deadlines?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes;General Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes
reference_answer: First review the grade with the professor: a review period of at least 48 hours is set aside after final grades are communicated. Then the student may file a written substantiated appeal with the academic heads within no more than five (5) working days after the review period concludes. It goes to the Bachelor's Appeals Board, which does not include the professor concerned, and its decision is final.

question: How do the attendance rules differ between a bachelor course and a master's subject?
expected_source: Attendance Policy Bachelor Degrees 2026-2027;General Academic Regulations for Master Degree Programmes
reference_answer: For bachelor courses, attendance is mandatory and expected at 100%, and below 80% means a 0.0 in both calls. For master's subjects, the general rule is at least 80% attendance, but the master's directors may require a different level (lower, higher or 100%), and the consequences of falling short are defined in each subject's syllabus.

question: A bachelor student fails a core course in both the ordinary and the extraordinary calls. What happens next, and when would they be unable to continue?
expected_source: General Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes;General Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes
reference_answer: The student must enrol on the course again the following academic year; a course can be taken for at most two consecutive years, giving four examination sessions (ordinary and extraordinary each year). If still not passed, the student may exceptionally ask the Rector for a single additional examination session, which is not automatic. If the course is still not passed, the student cannot continue in the bachelor programme.

question: I have a court summons on the day of a bachelor exam. Is my absence justified and can I take the exam another day?
expected_source: Attendance Policy Bachelor Degrees 2026-2027;General Academic Regulations for Bachelor Degree Programmes
reference_answer: An official summons to testify before a court or the police is a justified absence if supported by official documentation submitted through the Virtual Help Desk within seven days. Under the regulations, a student unable to sit a scheduled assessment instrument for sufficiently substantiated exceptional reasons may request to do it on a different day and time with the authorisation of the academic heads. Without justification the student gets 0.0 for that instrument.

question: Can my professor ban AI in a course, and what happens if I use it anyway?
expected_source: Student Guidelines for Appropriate Use of AI;The Student Code of Conduct
expected_location: IE University's position on AI in learning (p. 1) and What happens if you misuse AI? (p. 4);III.1.1
reference_answer: Yes. Faculty may restrict or prohibit AI for certain learning environments or assignments, and each course's AI policy is in its syllabus. Using AI when explicitly prohibited is treated as academic misconduct such as plagiarism or cheating, reviewed under the Student Code of Conduct, which lists doing academic work with AI support when not allowed by the professor as plagiarism, a serious infraction.

question: How long can an academic integrity case take, and how long do I have to appeal the decision?
expected_source: The Student Code of Conduct;The Student Code of Conduct
expected_location: II.3.1 i. Length of the process;III.3.1 ii a), ii b), ii d)
reference_answer: Every effort will be made to conclude any process within thirty (30) business/academic days of receipt of a complaint, extendable in exceptional circumstances; the AE Committee communicates its decision within fourteen (14) business/academic days of its meeting. An appeal must be presented within five (5) business/academic days of notification, and the appeal body resolves it within a further ten (10) business/academic days.

question: If a master's student's attendance falls below 80% in a subject, what grade do they get in the ordinary call, and can they still take the extraordinary call?
reference_answer: The documents do not give a master's-specific attendance policy. Art. 15.3 of the master's regulations only says the consequences are defined in each subject's syllabus. The bachelor policy (0.0 in both calls) is for bachelor programmes and should not be applied to master's students. The assistant should say it cannot confirm and point to the syllabus or Program Management.

question: Is a documented job or internship interview a justified absence for a master's student?
reference_answer: The documents do not say for master's students. Art. 15.4 of the master's regulations only says master's directors assess justified reasons case by case. The justified-absence list in the bachelor policy applies to bachelor programmes. The assistant should say it cannot confirm for master's and point to Program Management.

question: In a live online session of my master's programme, do I have to keep my camera on?
reference_answer: The documents do not give a camera rule for master's students. The camera rule appears only in the bachelor attendance policy. The assistant should say it cannot confirm for master's and suggest checking with Program Management or the syllabus.

question: After I submit documents for an absence in my master's, how long until I get the decision on whether it is justified?
reference_answer: The documents do not say for master's students. The 72-hour notification appears only in the bachelor attendance policy. The assistant should say it cannot confirm for master's and point to Program Management.

question: I am absent from a master's in-person class but join it online. Am I still marked absent, and can I take that day's exam?
reference_answer: The documents do not say for master's students. The rule appears only in the bachelor attendance policy. The assistant should say it cannot confirm for master's and point to Program Management.

question: How do I report a harassment incident at IE, and where do I send it?
expected_source: Code for the Prevention of Harassment in the Workplace
expected_location: Procedure in case of harassment, step 1
reference_answer: Report it by email or letter to the Diversity Commission, including a list of the facts, at ComisiondeDiversidadeIgualdad@ie.edu. The procedure can be started by the person harassed or by any witness.

question: In an informal harassment procedure, how soon must the Diversity Commission meet the parties, and how long does it have to produce its report?
expected_source: Code for the Prevention of Harassment in the Workplace
expected_location: Interviewing the parties involved; Preparation and content of the report
reference_answer: The Commission must meet the parties within a maximum of 5 days of the verbal or written complaint, and must prepare its report within a maximum of 3 working days after the interviews. The report states the results and a proposed solution or a recommendation to open formal proceedings.

question: What conditions must be met for behavior to count as moral harassment (mobbing) under the harassment code?
expected_source: Code for the Prevention of Harassment in the Workplace
expected_location: Categories of behavior subject to sanction, section D
reference_answer: The hostile or intimidating behavior must be systematic (at least once a week), over an extended period (more than 6 months), and in the workplace or an extension of it.

question: What share of IE's waste is recycled or reused, and who is the final waste processor?
expected_source: IE University Environmental Policy
reference_answer: Waste is outsourced to the waste management company Grupo Defesa, whose procedures are certified with the Zero Waste stamp. More than 95% of the waste that enters its plants is recycled or reused rather than sent to landfill.

question: How did IE's carbon footprint change while the student population grew between 2020-2021 and 2023-2024?
expected_source: Climate and Sustainability Plan
reference_answer: The student population grew by 64%, while the absolute carbon footprint fell by 28% and emissions per student fell by 56% over the same period.

question: What supplier sustainability target does IE set for 2030, and how much of its purchasing meets recognised standards today?
expected_source: Climate and Sustainability Plan
expected_location: 2. Sustainable Campus Operations, KPIs and Achievements
reference_answer: The target is that 60% of suppliers meet verified sustainability standards by 2030. The plan reports that 45% of purchasing currently meets recognised environmental and ethical standards.

question: Who can start a harassment complaint at IE, and what does IE say about who may investigate it?
expected_source: Code for the Prevention of Harassment in the Workplace;IE Equal Opportunities and Diversity Plan
reference_answer: The procedure can be started by the person allegedly harassed or by any person who witnessed the behavior (harassment code). The Equal Opportunities Plan adds that investigations respect all parties' privacy and the people investigating must have no previous connection with any of the parties.

question: Which initiatives do IE's policy documents use to cut single-use containers and food waste on campus?
expected_source: IE University Environmental Policy;Climate and Sustainability Plan
expected_location: Use of plastic or disposable items; Waste disposal;2. Sustainable Campus Operations, Achievements
reference_answer: Bumerang provides loaned reusable food containers (introduced with the cafeteria provider DoEat) to cut disposable take-away containers, and Too Good To Go redistributes leftover perishable cafeteria food at a discounted price. Both documents describe these two partnerships.

question: What was IE University's total greenhouse gas emissions in tonnes of CO2 in 2024?
reference_answer: The documents do not give an absolute figure. The Climate and Sustainability Plan only gives percentage changes (28% absolute reduction, 56% per student reduction), so the assistant should say it cannot find the figure.

question: How many harassment complaints did the Diversity Commission receive last year?
reference_answer: The documents do not say. The harassment code only states that the Commission keeps a confidential register of complaints, with no figures, so the assistant should say it does not know.
